"Trafficked"

By: Jacqui Jayamaha | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
In 2018, some may consider the idea of Modern Day Slavery, a terrible myth; the reality is this sordid practice is not only real, but also happening in ever increasing waves in South Africa.

Unique Selling Point:
Modern Day Slavery, the illegal trade of human beings, is real‚ hidden in plain sight and tearing at the social fabric of the nation as the demand for cheap labour and sexual services keeps growing. Durban is a perfect source for the supply and demand of trafficked victims, both male and female. Termed Modern Day Slavery, the sordid practice which is growing daily. Children, women and men are simply taken, transported, sold and abused, with coercion, abduction, fraud and deception being the common denominators. Victims that are rescued from the hands of their cruel captors, often take a lifetime to heal and rehabilitate while more like them are tricked and trapped daily. Human trafficking is indiscriminate as victims both male and female are sourced from all socio economic and racial groups in SA.


Summary:
We look at the case of Miguel Louw abducted from outside his school. Human trafficking is on the increase in SA and Miguel is just one case of many children that get caught up in a trafficking Syndicate. His abductor is in custody. His mother and Uncle have agreed to talk to us.
Zama was lured into a sex trafficking syndicate at the age of 12 and was rescued 6 years later from a Lodge in Durban. Her abductors received life imprisonment which is part of the legislation.
Advocate Dawn Coleman comments on the Legislation and penalties for human trafficking.
Nxo's little girl was abducted from church on New Year's day. She has not been seen for 6 months. Her father cries each day for his child.
Col. Mbehle is the spokesperson for missing children SAPS. She will answer questions about the Police procedures and cols cases etc.

Press Release:


Miguel Louw
A ten-year-old KZN boy disappears without a trace, a suspect is arrested and charged with trafficking, but almost a month after his abduction, the whereabouts of Miguel Louw, are still unknown. Experts believe that Miguel’s case isn’t unique and he’s just one of the hundreds of men, women and children, who are taken by human trafficking syndicates and illegally traded on the black market.
Producer: Jacqui Jayamaha
Presenter: Devi Sankaree Govender


Script:


TRAFFICKED

V/O This child has been missing for over 4 weeks – his family are desperate for his safe return.

Raylene “Plea for return of her child…”.

LINK “On the 17th of July this year, Durban mother, Raylene Louw said goodbye to her 10 year old son, Miguel, as he left for his daily short walk to Rippon Road Primary School, in Sydenham. For Raylene, it was a day just like any other except Miguel didn’t return home.

Raylene describes interaction with Miguel before he left for school

V/O Miguel’s home is less than 500 meters from his school, just a minute's walk.

V/O A month on, Louw’s life is at a standstill.

Devi “How long has it been since Miguel disappeared?
Raylene “It’s been a month now, since the 17th of July”
Devi “Interview …………………….
Raylene “……………….

LINK “It’s alleged that the little boy was taken around quarter past two in the afternoon from outside the gates of his school, located less than a minute from his home‚ what actually happened to Miguel that afternoon?

V/O Miguel’s Uncle, Bradley Benjamin, walked us through the events believed to have taken place that afternoon”
Bradley Benjamin’s walk through visuals and voice ….."

V/O “The suspect took Miguel to the nearby KFC. CCTV footage shows Miguel and the man getting a take away – they then leave the shop. The suspect is then seen leading the boy into a taxi and that was the last time he was seen.

V/O The court ordered that the 44 year old suspect cannot be identified. He was arrested in Central Durban; 3 days after Miguel went missing. He denied any knowledge of the boy’s abduction. At his first court appearance, in the Durban Magistrates court, Miguel’s mother wept as she demanded he tell her where her son was”.

****BEEP THE SWEAR WORDS – The mother screaming at accused in court
Raylene Shouts at accused in Court (audio and Vis court)

V/O “The accused faces charges of Humantrafficking – a schedule 5 offence. This is the most serious type of offence – like murder and rape – human trafficking carries a maximum sentence of LIFE IMPRISONMENT. The man had worked with Louw and hired to do odd jobs around the family’s home. (Photo of suspect with face blurred ID concealed – Police charge sheet – Charge Human Trafficking in Red across it)
Devi “When you found out that he was
Raylene “I was so angry…."
Devi“Was he known to you?’
Raylene “ Yes etc….
Devi “Did Miguel know him etc…”
Raylene “Yes, I used to work with him and …children met him”
Devi“He is up for serious charges…”
Raylene ”Trafficking” He managed to get hold of my id document and my children’s birth certificates and my identity documents” (Photos Birth Certificates)

V/O The family believes the suspect must havegained access to the documents while doing handy work in their home. Experts say the possession of such documents point to cross border trafficking.

V/O With increasing numbers of children abducted, investigations indicate that the purpose is for human trafficking. Anyone can fall victim to trafficking - men, women and children. Victims are abducted,transported and sold for sexual exploitation, forced labour or human body parts.

V/O 21 year old mother “Zama” was just 12 years old when she was lured and eventually trafficked.

Zama “And we decided to go withhim, to his lodge and he told us he was in a flat but he lied.

V/O “Once inside the lodge, Zama began to panic”

Zama “When I got there I saw the girls were smoking rock – holding pipes and lights. (C/U fire, lighting pipe, smoke etc)
Oh my god, what’s going to happen now?

V/O “It’s common for syndicates to get their captives addicted to hard drugs to create dependency. In Zama’s case it was crack cocaine – she began to sell her body to pay for her daily fix”.

Zama “When a car is coming here you going to the car and speak to the man. After that you say R150 for a full house or R50 rand for a straight “f*** BEEEP” .

V/O Throughout her captivity Zama longed for her family.
Zama’s “I thought about comments about her Mum… I was so lost”

V/O With easy access to the harbour and airport, Durban is a transit point and hot bed for the supply and demand of victims.

Dawn – Kwazulu Natal has seen various types of Trafficking in persons and for various reasons. So for example we’ve seen trafficking for sexual exploitation, we’ve seen it for forced labour, for domestic servitude and we’ve seen it for removal of body parts. So most definitely Kwa Zulu Natal is a source for victims of trafficking but also a destination for trafficking for purposes of exploitation".

V/O Senior State Advocate, of the National Prosecution Authority, Dawn Coleman Malinga, was part of the team that drew up the Prevention and Combatting of Trafficking in Persons Bill. The Act, was signed into Law in July 2013.

V/O Besides legal and special crimes authorities working to combat this escalating atrocity, Dawn says the general public have an equally important contribution to make”.

Dawn – We believe that every government department, all faith based organisations, community based organisations have a role to play in trafficking in persons. The last strategic objective, is the prosecution component. The act says that a person is liable for R100 million Rand fine, including imprisonment or to imprisonment for life”.

V/O The three men who had trafficked Zama, received life imprisonment.

V/O At the Umgeni Community Empowerment Center, Thami Ntimbane works as social media manager and trawls the internet to find links between children and adults. Ntimbane warns of the many internet traps designed to lure in adults – such as attractive offers of modeling and acting jobs …he knows how easy it is to locate children”

Thami “A mistake One of the big mistakes talks about photos of kids etc for child porn…”

V/O “Ntimbane manages drama groups that go into schools to educate young people about the ever increasing dangers of trafficking in persons”

V/O From streets, to malls and even churches,South African children are not safe anywhere. Durban father Mxolisi Ngwane’s 3 year old daughter, Siphesihle, was seated next to her mother at a church service on New Year’s morning this year, when she was snatched as her mother stood up for prayer. No-one saw who took her.

Int Mxolisi father “She went missing, I got really scared / the police, (Photo of little girl)

Int Mxolisi father ………….. the pain is so bad”.

LINK For parents, not knowing the whereabouts of their children is traumatic, but worse still, is imagining what has happened to them, whether they are dead or still alive.

Devi “Do you believe that Miguel is still alive?"
Raylene“Yes………I would feel it, he’s out there”.

V/O KZN Police spokesperson Colonel Thembeka Mbehle says the Durban Central Police investigate numerous missing children’s cases.

Devi “As soon as a child goes missing, how soon should parents report it?”
Colonel Mbehle “ Missing now, call now etc”
Devi What are some of the reasons children go missing?
Colonel Mbahle “Sometimes we found the child…body part, raped, traditional healer..”

LINK “AS HOPES DWINDLES IN THE MIGUEL AND SIPHESIHLE CASES, THE SHOCKING REALITY OF THE INCREASE IN CHILD ABDUCTIONS IN OUR COUNTRY, IS SOMETHING WE NEED TO PRIORITISE.

Devi“If you could say something to Miguel now….?”
Int Raylene” I would tell him that I love him and that I miss him and that I won’t stop looking for him”. Am not going to give up, I’m going to find him
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Teasers/Promos – Trafficking

10 sec
“Our children are under threat of being targeted for the Human Trafficking Industry – we need to become acutely aware of this growing, atrocity and proactively educate our youth”. (Vis School shots of kids playing/ shots from Thami’s drama group)

15 sec
“A little boy goes missing, just a short distance from his school – where is 10 year old Miguel Louw who was abducted by a man known to his family – as the communities fears grow, his mother still waits in hope for her son to come home”. (Poster on Billboard) Close up of his face in pic, abductor photo mother waits by the window

15 sec
“Timing is crucial when reporting a missing person “Colonel Report the person missing immediately” The hunt is still on to find Miguel Louw”. (Poster Miguel, Up sound Colonel sound up about timing)

30 sec
“Outside the Durban magistrates court, community members gather to show support for the family of a little boy who has been missing for over a month. A man known to Miguel Louw’s family stands charged for Human Trafficking, as the distraught mother begs him to tell her where her son is “Sound up mother in court”.(Beep out swearing) (Bill boards held by community, accused in pic ID covered, court logo on wall and Raylene begs the accused)

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): In 2018, some may consider the idea of Modern Day Slavery, a terrible myth; the reality is this sordid practice is not only real, but also happening in ever increasing waves in South Africa.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Modern Day Slavery, the illegal trade of human beings, is real‚ hidden in plain sight and tearing at the social fabric of the nation as the demand for cheap labour and sexual services keeps growing. Durban is a perfect source for the supply and demand of trafficked victims, both male and female. Termed Modern Day Slavery, the sordid practice which is growing daily. Children, women and men are simply taken, transported, sold and abused, with coercion, abduction, fraud and deception being the common denominators. Victims that are rescued from the hands of their cruel captors, often take a lifetime to heal and rehabilitate while more like them are tricked and trapped daily. Human trafficking is indiscriminate as victims both male and female are sourced from all socio economic and racial groups in SA.
metadata.Summary: We look at the case of Miguel Louw abducted from outside his school. Human trafficking is on the increase in SA and Miguel is just one case of many children that get caught up in a trafficking Syndicate. His abductor is in custody. His mother and Uncle have agreed to talk to us. Zama was lured into a sex trafficking syndicate at the age of 12 and was rescued 6 years later from a Lodge in Durban. Her abductors received life imprisonment which is part of the legislation. Advocate Dawn Coleman comments on the Legislation and penalties for human trafficking. Nxo's little girl was abducted from church on New Year's day. She has not been seen for 6 months. Her father cries each day for his child. Col. Mbehle is the spokesperson for missing children SAPS. She will answer questions about the Police procedures and cols cases etc.
